neighbours.label: the word right after optative 'May' opening a wish or blessing (May the..., May your...), not 'May' the month
fire: Thank you all for coming. May the road rise to meet you.
We grieve with the family. May his memory be a blessing.
Congratulations on the wedding! May your home be full of laughter.
The service ended with a prayer. May the Lord bless and keep you.
Happy birthday, old friend. May your year be bright.
Rest now, brave soldier. May you find peace at last.
The bard raised his cup. May our swords never break.
Good luck on the journey. May the wind be at your back.
quiet: Thank you all for coming. In May the road was closed for repairs.
We grieve with the family. Last May his father passed away.
Congratulations on the wedding! Every May your garden looks lovely.
The service ended with a prayer. By May the church was full again.
Happy birthday, old friend. Since May your letters have been rare.
Rest now, brave soldier. Early in May you will go home.
The bard raised his cup. In May our swords were forged.
Good luck on the journey. That May the wind was strong.

notes: All top examples are the token after a wish-'May' (May the, May his, May your, May Our). Near misses use May as a month or a modal question.
